new.title: Play the classics at the Bonami game museum
new.desc: Bonami SpelComputer Museum holds thousands of consoles, home computers, arcade cabinets and pinball machines from the 1970s onwards, and most of them can actually be played.
new.tip: Budget more time than you think: the arcade hall and the pinball row are hard to leave.

new.title: Step into the Vrouwenhuis
new.desc: Built before 1680, this almshouse sheltered elderly women until 1984. Today it is a tiny museum where the guide tells of founder Aleida Greve, her quirky will and the gossip of the residents; the regents' room is the showpiece.
new.tip: You can only get in on a guided tour, so book a slot on the museum's agenda first.

new.title: Time-travel through Zwolle at ANNO
new.desc: ANNO is the city museum, set in the monumental Drostenhuis plus a new wing, bringing together Zwolle's archaeology, archives and museum collections under one roof.
new.tip: It doubles as a tourist information point, so it is a smart first stop to pick up walking routes.

new.title: Find Johannes Cele in his hidden courtyard
new.desc: Off the Papenstraat a small courtyard hides a statue of Johannes Cele, the founder of Zwolle's famous medieval school. Most shoppers walk straight past it.
new.tip: Look for the narrow passage between the house fronts; the courtyard is a quiet spot to sit for a moment.

new.title: Track down the last three wall towers
new.desc: The medieval wall once had 23 towers; only the Pelsertoren, the Wijndragerstoren and the Zwanentoren survive. One is now a B&B, another a beer pub.
new.tip: Walk the moat side of the old town and you can tick off all three in under an hour.

new.title: Drink a beugel beer inside a city tower
new.desc: Café 't Beugeltje fills the medieval Wijndragerstoren; most of its beers come in swing-top 'beugel' bottles and its canal terrace was once voted the best in Zwolle. The Zwolse mustard tradition also started in this tower.
new.tip: On a sunny afternoon grab a terrace seat by the water early, then order something with Zwolse mosterd on the side.

new.title: Taste the beer list at Het Refter
new.desc: In one of the oldest buildings in town, Het Refter pours around 20 special beers on tap and some 200 in bottles, with the Peperbus looming over the terrace.
new.tip: Ask for a tasting flight if you cannot choose; the house beers are a good place to start.

new.title: Graze the Saturday market on the Grote Markt
new.desc: On Saturdays the square around the Grote Kerk fills with stalls of cheese, fresh stroopwafels and seasonal produce. For many Zwollenaren it is the social outing of the week.
new.tip: Grab a warm stroopwafel and a chunk of aged cheese, then sit on the church steps to people-watch.

new.title: Take home a jar from Librije's Winkel
new.desc: Guests at three-star De Librije kept asking to buy the jellies, jams and dressings they were served, so in 2005 the restaurant opened its own shop in the former women's prison.
new.tip: A much cheaper taste of Jonnie Boer's kitchen than the restaurant; peek at the prison courtyard while you are there.

new.title: Pull on boots for the Laarzenpad
new.desc: The boots trail through the Vreugderijkerwaard floodplain runs about 5.6 km along the IJssel, past grazing cattle and a bird hide, through one of the richest river landscapes near the city.
new.tip: Wear wellies after rain; the start is near the Vreugdehoeve sheep farm and dogs are not allowed on the trail.

new.title: Walk the Assendorp mural route
new.desc: A street art route of about 7 km leads past 18 murals in Assendorp, from huge gable paintings to small, well-hidden pieces.
new.tip: Plan about two hours and finish on the Assendorperplein for a drink.

new.title: Wander the sculpture fields of Anningahof
new.desc: Former meadows on the edge of Zwolle became a sculpture park where work by around seventy contemporary Dutch sculptors stands among ponds, grassland and wildflowers, with a new selection every year.
new.tip: The exhibition runs roughly from late spring to autumn; check the dates before you cycle out.

new.title: Climb the Lebuïnuskerk tower in Deventer
new.desc: A narrow spiral stair of some 220 steps takes you to the second gallery of Deventer's Grote Kerk, with the IJssel, the Bergkwartier and the Salland countryside spread out below.
new.tip: The tower opens on weekends in the warmer months; buy your ticket in the church shop. Deventer is about 25 minutes from Zwolle by train.

new.title: Stand on the vanished island of Schokland
new.desc: Schokland was an island in the Zuiderzee until the Noordoostpolder was drained around it. The low ridge, its church and the old sea wall became the first UNESCO World Heritage Site in the Netherlands.
new.tip: Start at Museum Schokland in the Middelbuurt, then walk along the former shoreline to feel how the island rises above the polder.

new.title: Stroll the gardens of Twickel near Delden
new.desc: Twickel is one of the great country estates of the Netherlands, with a moated castle, formal gardens, an orangery and dozens of protected farmhouses spread around Delden.
new.tip: In summer the orangery has a tearoom and the vegetable gardens open on set days; the castle interior is only shown for a short spell in August.

new.title: Visit Rijksmuseum Twenthe in Enschede
new.desc: The largest art museum in the east of the country spans medieval manuscripts, Ruisdael landscapes, Impressionists and contemporary art, in the rebuilt Roombeek district.
new.tip: It is about a ten minute walk northeast of Enschede station; combine it with a stroll through Roombeek's new architecture.

new.title: Meet the 'Oude Grijze' in Oldenzaal
new.desc: The Romanesque Sint-Plechelmusbasiliek dates back to the 12th century, and its sturdy tower, nicknamed the 'Oude Grijze' (old grey one), carries a 49-bell carillon.
new.tip: Time your visit with a carillon recital and listen from the terraces on the square around the church.

new.title: Pay respects at the Canadian War Cemetery in Holten
new.desc: On the wooded slope of the Holterberg lie 1,393 Canadian soldiers who fell during the liberation of the Netherlands; the rows of white headstones under the pines are deeply moving.
new.tip: Visit the small visitor centre first for the soldiers' stories, then continue into the Sallandse Heuvelrug on foot.

new.title: Hear the storm cannon in Blokzijl harbour
new.desc: Blokzijl's tiny harbour is ringed by 17th-century merchant houses from its peat-trading days. The old cannon on the quay was never fired at enemies; it warned of storms and high water.
new.tip: Combine it with Giethoorn by bike or boat; it is a much quieter harbour to sit by on a summer evening.

new.title: Look out to sea with the Urk fishermen's memorial
new.desc: Near the lighthouse, the statue of a woman gazing over the water remembers the hundreds of Urk fishermen lost at sea. Offshore lies the Ommelebommelestien, the rock where, locals tell their children, babies come from.
new.tip: Walk here from the harbour along the dyke; the names on the memorial wall show how many families the sea has touched.

new.title: Order a De Wereld beer in the Stomme van Campen
new.desc: Kampen once had dozens of breweries; De Wereld is the only one left, and its beer is poured in the Stomme van Campen, often called the brownest café in town.
new.tip: Afterwards walk to the Voorstraat, where the De Olifant factory still rolls cigars, a reminder of the hundred cigar makers Kampen once had.

new.title: Sip coffee at De Pelikaan in Zutphen
new.desc: De Pelikaan has been roasting coffee and selling tea since 1816 and is a royal warrant holder. Its old-fashioned shop has a small schenkerij where you drink the house blends with something sweet.
new.tip: Take a bag of a house blend home; Zutphen is about 45 minutes from Zwolle by train along the IJssel.

new.title: Drink a town beer at Cambrinus in Zutphen
new.desc: Hanseatic Zutphen had around forty breweries; Stadsbrouwerij Cambrinus in the heart of town is the one that survived, with a dark, medieval-feeling interior.
new.tip: Try the house brews after a walk past Zutphen's towers and hofjes.

new.title: Pick up chocolates under Hattem's Dijkpoort
new.desc: Right at the foot of the 14th-century Dijkpoort, chocolate studio A3 makes its own bonbons in the little walled town that also hosts a chocolate festival every other year.
new.tip: Cycle over from Zwolle via the IJssel bridge and pair it with the Voerman Museum's paintings of Hattem skies.

new.title: Taste Twente beer at the brewery in Hengelo
new.desc: The Twentse Bierbrouwerij brews in the old Hazemeyer factory buildings, and its tasting room pours ten Twente-brewed specialty beers alongside dishes made with local products.
new.tip: On Saturdays there is a small tour of the brewing lab; reserve in advance.

new.title: Hunt for books at the Deventer Boekenmarkt
new.desc: On one Sunday in early August, hundreds of stalls line the IJsselkade and the old streets of Deventer for what is billed as the largest book market in Europe.
new.tip: Arrive early by train; by midday the quay is packed. Bring a sturdy bag.

new.title: Board the Kamper Kogge
new.desc: This full-size replica of a 14th-century Hanseatic cog, modelled on a wreck found in the Flevopolder, is sailed by volunteers and in 2025 made it all the way to Visby in Sweden.
new.tip: The Koggewerf yard near the old centre is free to visit; ask about guided tours on board.

new.title: Go hofje hunting in Zutphen
new.desc: Behind Zutphen's street fronts hide almshouse courtyards built for the elderly, poor and widowed, the oldest being the Oude Bornhof from 1320. Ruitershofje, Agnietenhof and Luthers Hofje are other finds.
new.tip: Courtyards are lived in: go quietly, and finish with the Martinetsingel walk along the old walls.

new.title: Join the Vlöggelen in Ootmarsum at Easter
new.desc: On Easter Sunday and Easter Monday the eight Poaskearls lead a singing, hand-in-hand chain of townspeople through the streets, houses and cafés of Ootmarsum before the Easter fire burns.
new.tip: Anyone may join the line behind the Poaskearls; follow the crowd from the church and the Paaskamp fire in the late afternoon.

new.title: Watch the giant Easter fire of Espelo
new.desc: Around Holten, neighbourhoods compete each year for the biggest Easter fire; Espelo once built one of nearly 46 metres, a world record.
new.tip: Fires are lit on the evening of Easter Sunday; check which neighbourhood fires are open to visitors and dress for smoke.

new.title: See the flower parade in Vollenhove
new.desc: On the last Saturday of August, flower-covered floats roll through Vollenhove, the former Zuiderzee town once called the 'city of palaces'.
new.tip: Before or after the parade, walk to the old harbour and the remains of Castle Toutenburg.

new.title: Hike the heath of the Sallandse Heuvelrug
new.desc: Between Nijverdal and Holten rises a ridge of ice-age hills covered in vast heathland, topped by the Koningsbelt at 75 m, one of the highest points in the region.
new.tip: Start at the Staatsbosbeheer visitor centre in Nijverdal; come in late summer when the heather turns purple.

new.title: Walk the Eerde estate near Ommen
new.desc: The Natuurmonumenten estate around 18th-century Kasteel Eerde spreads over woods and the Besthmenerberg, where Krishnamurti once held his gatherings, along the Vecht valley.
new.tip: The castle is a school and cannot be visited, but the woods are open; the Pieterpad hiking trail also passes through Ommen.

fix.suggestion: Rename to Van der Velde in de Broeren in desc and set q to 'Van der Velde in de Broeren Zwolle'. The tip about going to the top floor still works (the third floor holds an exhibition).
